{{short description|Statistical physicist}}
'''Linda Elizabeth Reichl''' (born 1942){{r|born}} is a [[statistical physics|statistical physicist]] who works in the [[Center for Complex Quantum Systems]] at the [[University of Texas at Austin]],{{r|cqs}} and is known for her research on [[quantum chaos]].{{r|aps}}

==Education==
Reichl completed her Ph.D. in 1969 at the [[University of Denver]] with the dissertation ''Microscopic Theory of Quasiparticle Spin Fluctations in a Fermi Liquid''.{{r|mg}} She was advised by Elizabeth R. Tuttle and [[Ilya Prigogine]].{{r|pt}}

==Books==
Reichl's books include:
*''A Modern Course in Statistical Physics'' (University of Texas Press, 1980; 4th ed., Wiley, 2016){{r|mcsp}}
*''The Transition to Chaos: Conservative Systems and Quantum Manifestations'' (Springer, 1992; 2nd ed., 2004){{r|t2q}}

She is also the co-editor of several volumes of collected papers.

==Recognition==
Reichl became a [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]] in 2000 "for her original contributions to the field of quantum chaos".{{r|aps}}
